correctness.rationale: For each arbitrary mesh the Galerkin solution is exactly the interpolant of u=t(1-t)/2 by cell-average derivative orthogonality, so energy error is sum(h_j^3)/12. Dirichlet(1,...,1) moments give mean/variance, exponential representation gives CLT with variance 5/2. Empirical-CDF integration by parts and Poincaré prove n λ_min→π², isolated-small-exp edge decomposition proves λ_max/n²⇒2/Exp(1), hence κ/n³⇒2/(π²Exp(1)). Deterministic λ_min≥1/(n-1), λ_max≤4/h_min plus a fixed interior-collapse event give κ positive moments finite exactly below one. 550 exact rational Galerkin identities, 150 exact rational moment identities and finite numerical spectral probes passed when executed from supplied verify.py. No finite experiment is used as a proof of an infinite statement.

value.rationale: The model is a natural diagnostic of unconstrained random-node finite elements. It establishes exact finite-sample energy accuracy and variance, a nontrivial CLT, and a sharp infinite-mean stiffness-conditioning pathology with normalized Fréchet scaling, quantitatively contrasting the order n³ random system with order n² uniform meshes. This exposes a meaningful tradeoff between mesh randomness, approximation, and solver robustness, with direct motivation for mesh-quality safeguards; it is not a mere renamed elementary interpolation identity.
